dataset_provenance: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System)
key_findings: VIIRS detects 4.979x more active fire hot spots than MODIS (18.47M vs 3.71M), driven by its 375m spatial resolution.
MODIS records a significantly higher mean FRP (41.21 MW vs 9.68 MW) because smaller, cooler fires remain below the 1km MODIS detection threshold.
Integrated total radiated power is remarkably comparable: 152.8M MW for MODIS vs 178.8M MW for VIIRS (+17%), showing consistent energy estimation for major fires.
Both sensors exhibit peak diurnal fire activity in the early afternoon (12:00-14:00 UTC regional overpasses) matching peak ambient temperatures and lowest fuel moisture.
Data quality is exceptional: 22,175,332 out of 22,175,341 records (>99.9999%) are valid with zero missing coordinates or corrupt timestamps.
